verses.1: And it was in the month of Nisan, in the year 40 after Artaxerxes became king. I presented the crown to the king, and I did not act badly before him.
verses.2: And the king said to me, “Your face is sad, and you seem sick. But isn’t that because your heart is evil? I fear that you’re in great distress.”
verses.3: And he said to the king, “May the king live forever! May my face not be harmed. For the city of the tombs of my ancestors has been destroyed, and its gates have been burned by fire.”
verses.4: And the king said to me, “What do you seek here? Pray to the gods of heaven.”
verses.5: And he said to the king, “Is it good for the king to send me to Judah, to the city where my ancestors are buried?”
verses.6: And the king said to me, “The slave who sits at his side will accompany you until your death. After that, you will return. I was pleased with him, so I sent me away.” And I gave him a time limit.
verses.7: And he said to the king, “If it is good for the king, then let them give me provisions along the way across the river. They will take me there until I reach Judah.”
verses.8: And I was given custody of the treasury that belongs to the king. The king gave me trees for planting in the gates of the city, as well as for the protection of the city itself. And the king gave me these things as a gift from the good God.
verses.9: And I went over the river, and I delivered to them the messages of the king. The king sent with me officers and soldiers.
verses.10: And Sanbalat the Horonite and Tobiya, the servants of the people, heard about this. They suffered a great disaster. For it happened that a man came to ask for good for the children of Israel.
verses.11: And I will come to Jerusalem. There, I will stay for three days.
verses.12: And in the night, I and the men with me would stand up. But I didn’t tell anyone what God had given me to do for Jerusalem. And I wasn’t accompanied by any animals; I was alone, riding on that animal I was riding upon.
verses.13: And she went out through the gate of the city at night, towards the entrance of the Temple. She also went through the gates of Ashpoth. I was in Jerusalem’s streets, where the doors were burned by fire.
verses.14: And I will go through the gate of the eye, and also through the throne of the king. There is no place for the sheep to pass underneath.
verses.15: And I go up to the stream at night. And I return in the morning. I come back through the gate of the valley. And I return again.
verses.16: And the scribes did not know that I was going away, and what I was doing. To the Jews, priests, and all those who were in charge of the work, I still hadn’t told them yet.
verses.17: And he said to them, “Do you see the evil that is happening to us? Jerusalem is being destroyed, and its gates are burning in flames. Let us go and rebuild Jerusalem’s city. There will no longer be any more destruction.”
verses.18: And I will give them the hand of God, which is good to me. And also, the words of the king who said to me. They said, “May we be healed and may our children be strong.”
verses.19: And Sanbalat the Horonian and Tobiya, the servants of the Amonites, and Geshem the Arvians, heard this. They laughed at us and said, “What kind of words are these that you are saying to the king? You are plotting against him.”
verses.20: And I will answer them with words, and say to them: “The God of heaven will surely help us. We are His servants; we will be saved. But you have no part or share in this righteousness. You will have no honor or recognition in Jerusalem.”
